environment.description: Same Lambda container image deployed on EKS cluster (managed node group, Kubernetes 1.28). Namespace 'lambda-workloads' has Pod Security Standards label 'pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: baseline' applied at the namespace level. Additionally, a Kyverno ClusterPolicy 'restrict-header-injection' validates that all containers in the namespace must include the environment variable 'HEADER_SANITIZE_MODE=strict', which the application reads at startup to enable input sanitization on all header values (stripping \r\n characters). The pod spec includes this env var. The baseline Pod Security Standard prevents privileged escalation and hostPath mounts, ensuring the container cannot modify its own /proc/self/environ or bypass the sanitization by mounting host filesystem to alter runtime config. A NetworkPolicy restricts ingress to only the internal ALB controller pods (not raw NLB passthrough), and the ALB operates in HTTP mode with header value validation enabled (dropping requests with bare CR/LF in header-mapped query parameters).

config.request_path: ALB (HTTP mode, header validation) -> NetworkPolicy -> Pod (HEADER_SANITIZE_MODE=strict)
